title: How reference life tables shape comparisons of premature mortality from malignant CNS tumours across Europe (analysis code)
description:
Analysis code and derived data for a study of how the choice between national and common reference life tables changes age-standardised years-of-life-lost rates and country comparisons for the same recorded deaths, for malignant central nervous system neoplasms (ICD-10 C70-C72) in 28 European countries, 2012 to 2018, and eight comparison causes.

The pipeline combines Eurostat cause-of-death data with Human Mortality Database exposures, all-cause deaths and period life tables. It computes age-standardised years of life lost rates under national period life tables and two common references (the official GBD 2023 theoretical minimum risk life table and an empirical minimum-mortality table), the change in each country's rate between references, rank agreement between the resulting country orderings, the gap between the two countries of every reversed pair, the recurrence of each reversal across 2,000 Poisson replicates of the death counts, and the same comparison for eight further causes. A secondary analysis uses cause-deleted life tables to estimate the change in life expectancy at birth and in life disparity.

Human Mortality Database source files are not redistributable and are not included; an authenticated retrieval script and a manifest of series vintages and SHA-256 digests are provided instead. RESULTS_SUMMARY.md records the design and every headline result.
